title: Affine DVR square from a local domain in a finitely generated field
statement: Let $\varphi:B\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type, meaning that $C$ is generated by finitely many elements as a $B$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak r\subset C$ be a prime ideal, set $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak r)$, let $L=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, and write $\beta:C\to L$ for the residue map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $R\subseteq L$ be a Noetherian subring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a nonzero local integral domain and not a field, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R\ne0$. Suppose a unital homomorphism $\alpha:B\to R$ satisfies $(R\hookrightarrow L)\circ\alpha=\beta\circ\varphi$. Assume that the subfield of $L$ consisting of quotients of elements of $R$ is precisely the image of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ induced by $\varphi$, and put $\mathfrak p=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak m_R)$. Then there is a discrete valuation subring $A\subseteq L$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] containing $R$, with fraction field $L$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. For $u=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta):\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, $j=\operatorname{Spec}(A\hookrightarrow L)$, and $v=\operatorname{Spec}(B\xrightarrow{\alpha}R\hookrightarrow A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], one has $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ u=v\circ j$ and $v(s_A)=\mathfrak p$, where $s_A$ is the point corresponding to the maximal ideal of $A$. Here an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors, $\kappa(\mathfrak a)=D_{\mathfrak a}/\mathfrak aD_{\mathfrak a}$ for a prime $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $D$, and a fraction field consists of all quotients $r/s$ with nonzero denominator.

proof.text: Put $K=\{r/s\in L:r,s\in R,\ s\ne0\}$, the fraction subfield of $R$ in $L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated] to $\varphi:B\to C$ and $\mathfrak r$: its contracted prime is exactly $\mathfrak q$ and its finite-type hypothesis is given. Thus $L=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is generated as a field by finitely many elements over the image of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The assumed equality of that image with $K$ gives $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$.

source.place: Tag 0CM2, limits-lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian, proof: finite generation over the fraction field of R.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-domain-fg-field-dvr] to the given local domain $R$ and the actual subfields $K\subseteq L$ from step 1. The ring $R$ is Noetherian, nonzero and not a field by hypothesis, $K$ consists of its quotients by construction, and $L/K$ is finitely generated by step 1. We obtain a discrete valuation subring $A\subseteq L$ containing $R$, with every element of $L$ a quotient of elements of $A$, and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. These are exactly the required ring and fraction-field properties.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, applied with L equal to the source residue field as in Tag 0CM2.

proof.text: Let $i:R\hookrightarrow A$, $\ell:A\hookrightarrow L$ and $h=i\circ\alpha:B\to A$. The given compatibility says $\ell\circ h=(R\hookrightarrow L)\circ\alpha=\beta\circ\varphi$, as ring homomorphisms. By the contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta\circ\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\ell\circ h)=\operatorname{Spec}(h)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\ell)=v\circ j$. This proves the square commutes as scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CM2, limits-lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian, proof: final displayed diagram; Schemes Tag 01I2, schemes-lemma-category-affine-schemes, for functoriality.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], applied to $h:B\to A$ and $Q=\mathfrak m_A$, the image under $v=\operatorname{Spec}(h)$ of the point $s_A$ is the prime $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)$. For every $b\in B$, one has $h(b)\in\mathfrak m_A$ if and only if $\alpha(b)\in\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Consequently $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak p$, proving $v(s_A)=\mathfrak p$.
